question.problem:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below. 

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ x, & 0\le x\le 1 \\ 1, & x>1\end{aligned}\,\,{F}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & y<0 \\ y, & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 1, & y>1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs ${F}_{X}(x)$ and ${F}_{Y}(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)={F}_{X}(x)\cdot {F}_{Y}(y).
$$

Therefore, for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & ={F}_{X}(x)\cdot {F}_{Y}(y) \\  & =x\cdot y \\  & =xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0\text{ or }y<0 \\ xy, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ x, & 0\le x\le 1,\,y>1 \\ y, & x>1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 1, & x>1,\,y>1\end{aligned}
$$
